title: Zero-Cost Jamstack: GitHub Pages, Hugo CI/CD & Cloudflare Edge
subtitle: Automated static site generation pipeline with Hugo, GitHub Actions multi-branch deployments, and Cloudflare Anycast CDN caching.

overview.summary: This architecture implements a modern, enterprise-grade Jamstack publishing engine with zero infrastructure hosting costs. Authors write clean Markdown on local machines, push to a GitHub source repository, and trigger an automated GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline. The pipeline uses the Hugo Extended static site generator to compile static assets, XML sitemaps, RSS feeds, and a CNAME record into a dedicated publish branch (`gh-pages`). Cloudflare DNS manages domain routing, SSL termination, and Anycast CDN edge caching to serve global readers with sub-15ms First Contentful Paint (FCP).
overview.problemStatement: Traditional dynamic CMS platforms (e.g. WordPress, Drupal) introduce perpetual server hosting fees, database maintenance overhead, caching complexities, and severe security vulnerabilities (SQL injection, plugin exploits). This architecture replaces dynamic server compute with pre-rendered static assets delivered globally via Edge CDNs at zero recurring infrastructure cost.
corePrinciples: Pure Jamstack Pre-rendering: 100% of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and sitemaps are pre-compiled at build time.
Multi-Branch Source/Publish Separation: Keep Markdown draft sources and theme assets on `main` while deploying production build artifacts to `gh-pages`.
Automated GitOps Publishing: A single `git push` triggers automated linting, compilation, minification, and deployment.
Edge-First Anycast Delivery: Cloudflare CDN caches static files globally, offloading 99%+ of requests from origin servers.
Immutable Security Posture: Static files have zero database or backend runtime attack surface.

data.label: GitHub Actions Runner
data.subtitle: Hugo Extended CI/CD Builder
data.description: Ephemeral Linux CI/CD runner that checks out the repository, executes Hugo Extended to compile Markdown into static assets, generates sitemaps, and pushes artifacts to `gh-pages`.
responsibilities: Checks out source repository and theme submodules
Executes `hugo --minify --gc` to generate HTML, CSS, JS, and images
Generates XML sitemaps, RSS feeds, robots.txt, and OpenGraph tags
Generates `CNAME` file containing custom domain string
Commits and deploys `public/` build output to `gh-pages` branch
failureModes: Hugo template syntax error or broken shortcode halts pipeline
Invalid front-matter date or unclosed Markdown tag

configSnippet.code:
name: Deploy Hugo Site to Pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: true
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Setup Hugo
        uses: peaceiris/actions-hugo@v3
        with:
          hugo-version: 'latest'
          extended: true
      - name: Build
        run: hugo --minify --gc
      - name: Deploy to gh-pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v4
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: ./public
          publish_branch: gh-pages
          cname: techflow.io

data.label: GitHub Pages Branch
data.subtitle: Branch: gh-pages (Published Site)
data.description: Orphan Git branch containing solely the compiled static production bundle (HTML, CSS, JS, sitemap.xml) and root CNAME record for GitHub Pages web engine.
responsibilities: Holds production-ready static assets built by GitHub Actions
Houses root `CNAME` file containing target custom domain
Acts as the deployment source branch for GitHub Pages
failureModes: Accidental manual overwrite prevented via branch protection rules

data.label: GitHub Pages Origin
data.subtitle: Static Web Server & TLS Proxy
data.description: GitHub Pages web serving infrastructure. Resolves domain mapping from CNAME file, handles Let's Encrypt TLS certificates, and serves pre-rendered static files.
responsibilities: Maps incoming HTTP host headers to the corresponding `gh-pages` repository
Provides automatic origin TLS termination and HTTPS redirection
Serves static assets and handles 404 fallback page routing
Acts as the secure origin server for Cloudflare CDN edge
failureModes: Origin rate limits during massive traffic spikes (mitigated by Cloudflare CDN cache)

data.label: Cloudflare Edge CDN & DNS
data.subtitle: Global Anycast DNS & Edge Cache
data.description: Authoritative DNS and Edge Content Delivery Network. Manages one-time CNAME/A records pointing to GitHub Pages, terminates TLS (Full Strict), and caches static assets at 330+ edge locations.
responsibilities: Authoritative DNS resolution (CNAME: `techflow.io` -> `<username>.github.io`)
Global Anycast edge caching for HTML pages, CSS, JS, images, and fonts
Delivers instant First Contentful Paint (FCP) and 99%+ origin offload
HTTP/3 QUIC transport and modern Brotli asset compression
Enterprise DDoS mitigation and web application firewall protection
failureModes: Stale edge cache after new publish (mitigated by automated cache purge webhook or short HTML TTL)

configSnippet.code:
# Cloudflare DNS Records
Type:  CNAME
Name:  @ (or www)
Target: username.github.io
Proxy: Proxied (Orange Cloud ON)

# Edge Cache Rules
- HTML Pages: Cache TTL 4 Hours (Edge Cache-Control)
- Assets (.css, .js, .png): Cache TTL 1 Year (Immutable)
- SSL/TLS Mode: Full (Strict)

tradeoffs.decision: GitHub Pages + Hugo Jamstack vs. Traditional Dynamic CMS (WordPress / Ghost on EC2/VPS)
tradeoffs.chosenApproach: Static Site Generation (Hugo) hosted on GitHub Pages with Cloudflare Edge CDN
pros: Zero Ongoing Hosting Cost: $0/month infrastructure on GitHub Pages + Cloudflare Free Tier forever
One-Time DNS & SSL Configuration: Cloudflare handles Anycast routing and automatic Full Strict HTTPS
Superior SEO & Automated Sitemaps: Hugo automatically generates canonical URLs, OpenGraph social cards, XML sitemaps, and RSS feeds
Complete Theme & Layout Control: Full customization of HTML/CSS/JS without database plugins or CMS bloat
Client-Side Content Speed & Security: Pure static files eliminate SQL injections, PHP vulnerabilities, and backend exploits
Frictionless Authoring Workflow: Write in standard Markdown, version control every post in Git with branch protection
Ultra-Fast First Page Paint: Cloudflare Global Anycast Edge CDN caches assets within 15ms of 95% of world population
cons: No Server-Side Dynamic Compute: Cannot execute server-side PHP/Node/Python scripts; dynamic features like comments, search, or forms require client-side third-party APIs (e.g. Giscus, Algolia, Formspree) or serverless functions
Rebuild Required for Content Updates: Every change requires a ~30-45s GitHub Actions CI/CD compile and push cycle before going live
rejectedAlternatives: WordPress on AWS EC2 / DigitalOcean ($15-60/mo hosting, MySQL maintenance, security patching, plugin bloat)
Ghost CMS on Docker VPS ($10-30/mo, database backup management, memory overhead)
Static Site with AWS S3 + CloudFront (High complexity, CloudFront data egress costs, manual IAM setup)

tradeoffs.decision: Static Site Generator: Hugo vs. Gatsby / Next.js Static Export vs. Jekyll
pros: Blazing Fast Compilation: Builds 1,000+ pages in under 250ms (50x faster than Jekyll and Node-based SSGs)
Zero Node.js Dependency Hell: Single binary with zero `node_modules` vulnerabilities or breaking npm updates
Native Asset Pipelines: Built-in SCSS/SASS transpilation, PostCSS, asset fingerprinting, and image resizing
cons: Go Template Syntax: Requires learning Golang `html/template` syntax instead of JSX/React
rejectedAlternatives: Jekyll (Ruby dependencies, slow build times for large sites > 500 pages)
Next.js SSG Export (Heavy JavaScript client hydration bundle, frequent major version migrations)

securityAndCompliance.implementation: Cloudflare enforces Full (Strict) SSL with GitHub Pages origin certificates, automated HTTP to HTTPS redirection, and strict HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) headers.

securityAndCompliance.area: Zero Attack Surface (Immunized from Backend Exploits)
securityAndCompliance.implementation: Without dynamic server runtimes, databases, or server-side interpreters (PHP/Python/Node), the architecture is naturally immune to SQL injection, remote code execution (RCE), and server-side request forgery (SSRF).
Cloudflare Anycast absorbs multi-terabit volumetric DDoS attacks at edge data centers without traffic ever reaching GitHub Pages origin servers.
GitHub `main` and `gh-pages` branches enforce protected status with required status checks, preventing unauthorized direct pushes and ensuring cryptographic commit provenance.
